text: When manufacturing conditions change, yesterday's model can stop being reliable.
REFLEX explores a different question: when should a small local model ask for a new measurement?
This is real local inference on public semiconductor research data.
Each prediction happens before its measurement.
When a measured result surprises the model, REFLEX shortens the sampling interval.
As the process stabilizes, it measures less often.
The model updates locally, with no cloud calls.
Here, eighty-eight measurements cover five hundred and forty-two recorded samples.
We compare against the published GRAPE model at the same measurement count, and against measuring every sample.
The evidence view keeps those failures and both datasets visible.
The current prototype reuses GRAPE, with an event-triggered measurement schedule.
On dataset one, the exploratory schedule reduced error by twenty-three point four percent, at the same measurement budget.
Dataset two showed no clear advantage.
Delayed feedback also removed the first dataset's advantage.
Our next step is delay-aware adaptation, a fresh holdout, and a CMP data-validation partner.
